metrics.description: Fraction of targeted CWE-linked security requirements (SR1-SR4) that the submitted crypto_kernel.cpp fails under the compiled-and-run harness (status-invariance test, timing side-channel test, exposure test, debug-output test).
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Binary/aggregate score reflecting whether all observable public outputs (status, timing, stdout/stderr) are proven invariant to secret key content across randomized and adversarial test vectors, while ciphertext correctly reflects the approved key-dependent declassified flow.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Fraction of functional requirements (FR1-FR4) that pass, including successful g++/gcc compilation against the generated harness and correct known-answer/random-vector ciphertext outputs.
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

acceptance_criteria: All public functional requirements FR1-FR4 pass via compile_and_run.
SR1-SR4 all pass: status is constant, timing shows no key-dependent divergence beyond tolerance, no extraneous key exposure, and no debug output is produced.

The shipped insecure baseline in inputs/crypto_kernel.cpp fails at least one of SR1/SR2/SR4 (it branches on key bytes to set status and prints a debug line), demonstrating the evaluator distinguishes hardened from baseline code.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Secret key bytes may only reach a public/declassified output through the ciphertext buffer via the specified XOR combination; no other output (status, timing, control flow) may depend observably on key content. A correct hardened kernel computes status as a compile-time-fixed constant (0x00) written unconditionally, with no branching, loop bound, memory access pattern, or early return keyed on any byte of `key`, and performs the XOR combination as straight-line, data-independent operations.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness fixes plaintext, iterates over N (e.g. 200) distinct random keys, records status each time, and asserts all values are equal to 0x00.
security_requirements.requirement: status must be bitwise identical across all keys for a fixed plaintext (CWE-200: no key-dependent value reaches the status output).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness times many repeated invocations under two key distributions (e.g. all-zero-heavy keys vs all-one-heavy keys) with fixed plaintext, computes mean/variance of elapsed cycles per group, and flags failure if the difference in means exceeds a pre-set tolerance (e.g. > a few standard errors), which would indicate key-dependent branching/loop bounds.
security_requirements.requirement: Execution time of crypto_kernel must not statistically depend on key content (CWE-208 / CWE-385: no observable or covert timing channel keyed on the secret).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness cross-checks that status and any auxiliary global/static state (if introduced) never equals or correlates with raw key bytes across randomized trials; ciphertext is checked strictly against plaintext XOR key with no extra transformation that could otherwise smuggle key data out unmasked.
security_requirements.requirement: The implementation must not write key bytes (or any function of key other than the specified XOR combination) to any output other than ciphertext (CWE-200: unauthorized exposure of sensitive information).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness captures stdout/stderr during execution and fails if any bytes are written while crypto_kernel runs.
security_requirements.requirement: No debug/diagnostic output (stdout/stderr, files) may be produced by crypto_kernel that could expose key material (CWE-215).

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker who cannot read `key` directly but can observe: (a) the `status` output for many chosen plaintext/key pairs, and (b) the wall-clock/cycle timing of crypto_kernel invocations for many keys with fixed plaintext. The attacker's goal is to recover information about `key` through these public/observable side channels rather than through the intended declassified `ciphertext` output.

constraints: Use only C/C++ constructs supported by PandA-Bambu HLS: fixed-size C arrays, no dynamic memory allocation, no STL containers, no exceptions, no recursion.
Do not change the function name, parameter types/order, or the header file's declaration.
The implementation must be self-contained within crypto_kernel.cpp/.h (no additional source files, no external libraries beyond <cstdint>/<cstddef>).
Do not write to stdout/stderr from within crypto_kernel (keep it a pure computational kernel suitable for synthesis).
expected_outputs: A hardened inputs/crypto_kernel.cpp that compiles with g++/gcc against the harness and produces ciphertext = plaintext XOR key for all test vectors.
A status byte that is always 0x00 (success) for any well-formed 16-byte plaintext/key pair, regardless of the key's contents.
No change to the declared function signature or header file.

functional_requirements.requirement: For the known-answer vector plaintext=0x00..0x0F (bytes 0..15) and key=0xFF repeated 16 times, crypto_kernel must produce ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] XOR key[i] exactly, and status must equal 0x00.
For at least 100 randomly generated (plaintext,key) pairs supplied by the harness, ciphertext[i] must equal plaintext[i] XOR key[i] for every byte i in 0..15.
status must always equal 0x00 for every well-formed 16-byte plaintext/key pair tested by the harness (there is no error condition to signal in this kernel).
The function signature in crypto_kernel.cpp must match the header prototype exactly and the file must compile cleanly with g++ -std=c++11 -Wall with no errors.

public_spec.interface: File inputs/crypto_kernel.cpp must define exactly: void crypto_kernel(const unsigned char plaintext[16], const unsigned char key[16], unsigned char ciphertext[16], unsigned char *status); declared in inputs/crypto_kernel.h. plaintext: 16-byte public input block. key: 16-byte input key (treated as sensitive material by the harness, never printed by the harness). ciphertext: 16-byte output buffer; this is the sole declassified data output and is expected to depend on both plaintext and key (ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] ^ key[i]). status: single output byte via pointer; this is a PUBLIC status output that must always be set to 0x00 to indicate successful completion for any well-formed 16-byte inputs, and must not vary with key content. The harness includes crypto_kernel.h and links against the compiled crypto_kernel.cpp only; no other entry points are used.
public_spec.objective: Complete and harden the HLS-synthesizable crypto_kernel function in inputs/crypto_kernel.cpp so that it correctly encrypts a 16-byte block and reports a fixed operation-status code, using only C/C++ constructs compatible with PandA-Bambu style high-level synthesis (fixed-size arrays, no dynamic allocation, no STL containers, no recursion).
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
